newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Petronas mulls southern African gas development.
newsitem.headline: Petronas mulls southern African gas development.

text.p: Malaysian state energy company Petroliam Nasional Berhad (Petronas) is considering the development of gas-based petrochemical industries in southern Africa with its partner Engen Ltd, senior vice president Dato' Hamzah Bakar said on Monday.

He told the Africa Oil 1996 conference that they were examining the potential of the considerable gas deposits in Namibia and Angola "to see if we can do something to give a base load for the first production of gas."
"Once we start then we can create the momentum for the development of a petrochemical industry in this region," he said.
Hamzah said Petronas had developed its own gas pipeline and petrochemical industries in Malaysia, using power generation as the baseload to get going.
"We see it as having potential here (as well) but because in South Africa gas cannot compete with coal for power generation, we have to find another baseload.
"There is potential for us to invest and develop but we have to find another baseload industry that will take care of the initial development of natural gas."
This would provide feedstocks to develop petrochemical industries.
There was particular potential in the development of a synthetic fibre industry "and we are looking at a possible venture in this area", Hamzah said.
Other potential areas included using gas to produce gasoline "which will solve some of your pollution problems" or as household gas.
He said Petronas, which has a 30 percent stake in Engen, was very interested in expanding in Africa, which he believed had great growth potential.
Apart from South Africa, energy demand in Africa was amongst the lowest in the world, "and so there is only one way to go, and that is to go upwards and expand."
"We are taking a long-term view. We want to be here at the very start so that when the expansion comes we will know the market place, we will know the people."
The move into Africa was being assisted by the fact that many countries were liberalising their economies and political stability had returned to many countries.
